actions: Use the stated current Canadian physical-region reference to identify the Canadian Shield, Hudson Bay Lowland and Great Lakes–StLawrence Lowlands as three actual landform regions in Canada. Locate them broadly on the national reference, then use the separate Ontario outline/reference to revisit their Ontario portions. Reading a reference is not a claim to an exhaustive seven-region national inventory.

Describe a major characteristic of each and compare at least one supported similarity and difference. Both lowland regions have generally low-relief landscapes, while the Hudson Bay Lowland’s wetland plain contrasts with the southern plain-like lowlands and local escarpment/hills. Contrast the Shield’s widespread rock, rounded terrain and many lakes with these lowland settings; no broad region is perfectly uniform.

Retain the COMPLETE unchanged topic assessment: after study, name and broadly locate the three regions on an Ontario outline without their labels, explain their distinguishing characteristics, account for checked local variation and recognize the pattern in a differently styled reference. Do not infer this knowledge merely from a labelled-map lookup.

Transfer to a changed Canadian reference/legend: locate the same selected regions and explain a supported similarity/difference without relying on one colour scheme or confusing a province with a physical region.
